transcript: I went to go see August wilson's The Piano Lesson. this is the last revival that I needed to see this year until A doll's House comes out, and I was really pleasantly surprised by this production. this, of course, is a star studded cast. you have Samuel L. Jackson, Daniel Brooks, John David Washington. Samuel L. Jackson has done 1t of theater, but this is the first time that I've seen him on stage, and he was absolutely spectacular. Danielle Brooks, though, is amazing in everything that she does, and I truly believe she'll get a nomination for this. I was really surprised by how much I love this production. I tend to enjoy all of August wilson's work, but sometimes it just takes me a while to get into it. I've seen 4 shows now in the Pittsburgh Cycle, and I think this one's my favorite. for those that don't know, August Wilson wrote 10 plays as part of the Pittsburgh Cycle. every single play takes place in a different decade. the Piano Lesson is the play in the 30s. tells a story of a brother and sister here played by Washington and Brooks, and the relationship to this piano that's part of their family. and there were so many twists and turns in this play. I had no idea where this play was going, and I. I definitely did not expect the ending. it's a little wild, but it's worth. it's worth going to. I did get a rush ticket to this. this was a partial view seat. that's all the props to. let Tanya Richardson Jackson, who directed this production, for directing with sightlines in mind. this is not the view from where I was sitting. this is from the aisle. but essentially, I missed anything that happened on this lower staircase or anytime somebody walked through the door. that you can't even see here. I miss some stuff that happened on the upper level. unless it happened towards the front of that section. for the most part, action didn't happen in those locations. at least anything that was important happened in view, which is the sign of a very strong director. it truly mostly happens around the couch and the table and the piano. but even then, I could see, even design wise. and important piece of this piano is that it's covered in carvings. and as you can see, they're not just on the front, which I cannot see, but also on the side. and y'all, I really loved this set. I love a good house set, and I thought this one was cleverly done. overall, I thought this was a really strong production. I don't think it's gonna get 1t of Tony love, because I think it will be overshadowed by Death of a Salesman and Top Dog Underdog that I just feel are stronger revivals. but there's so much to really love about this production. and fortunately, is the only one of those that is still open. piano Lesson is closing January 29th. so if you haven't seen it yet, you do have another week to do so. and I really recommend this one, especially if you're not familiar with August wilson's work. I think this is one of his best plays.
